name: HTML
summary: Structure accessible pages with semantic elements, links, media, tables, forms, and native controls.

lessons.title: Page structure and semantic regions
lessons.explanation: HTML gives content a structure. Use headings for a meaningful outline. Put the primary page content in main and related navigational links in nav. Save this example as a local .html file and open it in a browser.

api.name: <!doctype html>
api.description: Request modern standards mode in browsers.

api.name: <title>
api.description: Provide the document title shown in a tab or bookmark.

api.name: <main>
api.description: Identify the primary content of the page.

api.name: lang
api.description: Declare the language so assistive technology can read text appropriately.

lessons.practice: Add a section with a descriptive heading and a paragraph explaining the next task.
lessons.pitfall: Pick headings for structure. Use CSS to control their visual size.

lessons.title: Links, lists, and relative paths
lessons.explanation: A link uses href to identify a destination. A fragment such as #summary targets an element id in the same page. Relative paths are resolved from the current document when there is no base override.

api.name: <a href="...">
api.description: Create a link to a URL, file, or section.

api.name: <ol> / <ul>
api.description: Mark up an ordered or unordered list.

api.name: id
api.description: Assign a unique document identifier for fragments and other references.

lessons.practice: Create examples/loops.html beside the current page, then test both navigation links.
lessons.pitfall: Use descriptive link text so users know what will open. Each id must be unique.

lessons.title: Local images, captions, and responsive assets
lessons.explanation: An img provides an image and a text alternative. Use figure and figcaption when the image benefits from a visible caption. Provide the source image dimensions so the browser can reserve space before decoding.

api.name: alt
api.description: Describe useful visual information. Use an empty alt attribute for a decorative image.

api.name: width and height
api.description: Provide intrinsic dimensions so layout can reserve the correct aspect ratio.

api.name: srcset / sizes
api.description: Offer alternative image sources and describe the intended rendered width.

lessons.practice: Save a local image to the expected folder and revise the alternative text to describe your own image.
lessons.pitfall: A caption and an alt attribute serve different roles. Avoid needless repetition.

lessons.title: Tables, captions, and header relationships
lessons.explanation: Use a table for row-and-column data. A caption describes what the table contains. Header cells use th, and scope helps connect them to the relevant rows or columns.

api.name: <caption>
api.description: Name or summarize a data table.

api.name: <thead> / <tbody>
api.description: Group header rows and body rows.

api.name: <th scope="row">
api.description: Associate a header with the other cells in that row.

lessons.practice: Add a Date column and a third row. Verify that every data row has the same logical columns.
lessons.pitfall: Use CSS grid or flexbox for page layout. A table communicates relationships among data.

lessons.title: Labels, inputs, and form submission
lessons.explanation: A label connects visible text to an input and gives it an accessible name. A submitted input generally needs a name attribute. With GET, named fields are encoded in the URL query string.
lessons.example:
<form action="search.html" method="get">
  <label for="search">Search topics</label>
  <input id="search" name="q" type="search" required maxlength="80">
  <button type="submit">Search</button>
</form>

api.name: for and id
api.description: Associate a label with an input.

api.name: type / required / maxlength
api.description: Describe input and ask the browser to enforce basic constraints.

api.name: name
api.description: Identify the field in the submitted data.

api.name: method="get"
api.description: Send the form fields as URL query parameters.

lessons.practice: Create a search.html file and inspect the query string after submitting a term. The destination page needs code to interpret it.
lessons.pitfall: Client-side validation helps users. A backend must still validate any submitted data.

lessons.title: Native disclosure and keyboard access
lessons.explanation: Use elements with built-in interaction when possible. A button handles keyboard activation, and details exposes a disclosure control with a summary. Users can navigate interactive elements using Tab.

api.name: <details> / <summary>
api.description: Create a browser-managed disclosure widget.

api.name: <button type="button">
api.description: Create an action control that will not submit a form.

api.name: aria-label
api.description: Supply an accessible name when visible text cannot name the element.

lessons.practice: Test the disclosure by keyboard. Confirm that Tab focuses it and Enter or Space activates it.
lessons.pitfall: Avoid using a clickable div for a button. It lacks native keyboard and focus behavior.
